chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran and Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, altogether from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a woman who died and no one was known to be for her, and she had a husband. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The inheritance, all of it, is for her husband.' From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Yahya al-Halbi, from Ayub ibn al-Hurr, from Abu Baseer who said, 'I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he called for Al-Jami'a (the Book). So we looked into it, and therein was, a woman who died and left her husband, not having an inheritor for her other than him, for him was the wealth, all of it'.

key_terms.الْجَامِعَةُ: Al-Jami'a (a specific book of hadith attributed to Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: Who inherits a woman's estate if she dies with no known relatives except her husband?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi confirms the principle of 'al-mirath li-man qabila' (inheritance for the one who receives it), where the husband inherits the entire estate in the absence of other heirs, a ruling supported by both Imam al-Sadiq and Imam al-Baqir. This specific scenario highlights the completeness of the husband's share when the 'asabah' (residuary heirs) and 'dhawu al-furud' (fixed-share heirs) are absent, ensuring no portion of the estate remains unallocated.
